argv:
Rewrite the text following the Microsoft writing style.

Sound like a helpful colleague chatting with the reader, not a manual. Use
contractions everywhere they'd naturally occur, address the reader directly as
"you", and reach for everyday words over formal ones. A sentence fragment is
fine when it lands the point — don't force every thought into a full clause.

Open with the single thing the reader most needs to know, then explain. Keep
sentences short and let the page's shape (headings, short paragraphs) do some
of the work.

Use sentence case for any heading. Use the active voice and the present tense.
Tell the reader exactly what to do and what happens next, in a tone that feels
like a quick conversation rather than a document.

Skip jargon, hedging, and anything that talks down to the reader — but don't
skip the personality. A little warmth and a casual aside are welcome.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
The Millbrook Hollow City Council voted Tuesday night to approve an amended version of the parks and recreation line item, following a meeting that also touched on the long-delayed replacement of the Third Street bridge. According to a spokesperson for the mayor's office, the revised figure reflects "ongoing conversations" among council members, though the spokesperson declined to characterize those conversations further. A separate memo, attributed by two council staffers to the finance subcommittee, put the adjustment at approximately $340,000, a figure that a budget analyst who reviewed the memo said was "in the range we expected." Buried near the end of that same memo, and not raised by any council member during the meeting, was a line noting that the bridge's lead structural engineer had flagged a load-bearing crack serious enough to warrant closing the span to truck traffic within 90 days. The bridge project, which has appeared on the capital plan since at least 2019 and has already drawn 14 change orders, was not discussed in detail. Council member Dana Okafor, reached after the meeting, said only that "the process worked the way it's supposed to work, and I think residents should feel good about that."
</passage>

response.text:
Here's the real news buried in Tuesday's meeting: the Third Street bridge has a crack serious enough that engineers want trucks off it within 90 days. That detail showed up on the last page of a memo — and no council member brought it up out loud.

The meeting itself was about something else. The Millbrook Hollow City Council voted Tuesday night to approve an amended parks and recreation budget line. A mayor's office spokesperson said the new number reflects "ongoing conversations" among council members, but wouldn't say what those conversations actually covered.

Two council staffers pointed to a finance subcommittee memo that pegs the adjustment at roughly $340,000. A budget analyst who read the memo called that figure "in the range we expected."

Then there's the bridge. That same memo notes the lead structural engineer flagged a load-bearing crack — serious enough to close the span to truck traffic within three months. Nobody raised it during the meeting. The bridge itself has been sitting on the capital plan since at least 2019 and has racked up 14 change orders along the way, but it didn't get a real discussion Tuesday.

Council member Dana Okafor, asked about it afterward, kept things vague: "The process worked the way it's supposed to work, and I think residents should feel good about that."
